title: Gradual-release signal clarification and SLA-aware rollback matrix
creator: Priya Desai
description: Follow-up to the Feb 4th failed gradual rollout where a canary model caused intermittent latency spikes and generation regressions for a subset of routes. Goal: produce a compact, testable rollback matrix and tighten detection signals so future staged rollouts either auto-heal or rollback cleanly with minimal customer impact.
postmortem_summary: During the staged release of model:open-chat-x-v2 -> traffic split 5% canary, 95% prod, we observed correlated p95 latency increases and degradation in token-level perplexity for one routing rule (chat-long-context). The canary produced a small but consistent tokenization mismatch and higher KV cache miss amplification on certain sequence lengths, which increased average decode time and pushed request tail latency above SLOs. Monitoring alerts were noisy and ambiguous, delaying automated rollback. This ticket consolidates the learnings into an operational rollback matrix and implements clearer telemetry and safety checks.
root_cause: Model variant introduced behavior change for long sequences that increased KV cache churn and produced slightly different tokenization leading to higher per-token generation time plus occasional invalid structured outputs. Secondary cause: insufficient signal-to-noise in the canary detection pipeline (alerts based only on error-rate and qps).
detection_timeline: 2025-02-04 09:10 - Small p95 rise observed on route chat-long-context (+37%)
2025-02-04 09:12 - Alert triggered (latency > threshold) but no auto-rollback configured for combined latency+quality signal
2025-02-04 09:19 - Manual investigation: found KV cache miss rate spike and generation-perplexity drift for canary requests
2025-02-04 09:35 - Canary scaled back to 2% manually; subsequent manual rollback at 09:48
runbook_steps: Step 0: If any SLA route p95 exceeds 2x baseline for >3 minutes AND quality (perplexity or eval set BLEU/ROUGE equivalent) shows >10% regression -> trigger immediate partial rollback to last-stable-variant
Step 1: Query per-route telemetry: p50/p95/p99 latency, KV cache hit ratio, model decode time per token, tokenization error rate, structured-output schema errors
Step 2: Check cross-correlation windows: if latency and KV miss ratio rise together within 30s, escalate to mitigation and consider auto-rollback

Step 3: When rollback executes, run automated sanity smoke: 50 synthetic requests representing long-context, short-context, and structured-output routes; verify tokenization parity and enrichment correctness
Step 4: Post-rollback: capture 30 minutes of trace-level data and snapshot model logs; attach to incident thread and create follow-up PRs for any missing instrumentation
safety_checks: Canary traffic must include at least 1% of synthetic requests that exercise edge sequence lengths and structured tools to surface tokenization mismatches
Reject canary rollout if KV cache miss rate on canary > baseline+5% for more than 2 consecutive minutes during initial ramp
Require combined metric trigger (latency OR error-rate) PLUS quality regression metric (eval-set or online eval) to enable auto-rollback
Require a minimum telemetry sampling rate for p95 traces (>= 20 traces/min) on canary routes; otherwise pause rollout
rollback_matrix: Matrix rows: [impact dimension, detection signal, threshold, immediate action, cooldown]. Examples: (SLO latency, p95>2x baseline for 3m => auto-rollback to last-stable; Quality regression, online eval score drop >10% for 5m => pause rollout + notify on-call; Structural failures, schema error rate >0.1% => immediate rollback and alert). Cooldown default 30m after rollback before reattempt.
action_items: A1: Add tokenization parity synthetic checks to canary harness (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ci/pull/3334)
A2: Ship instrumentation for KV cache miss ratio per model-variant and route (ENG-51234 monitoring work)
A3: Implement combined detection rule in rollout controller: latency+quality gating and enable auto-rollback boolean flag
A4: Console: add 'canary health' widget showing combined-signal status and last rollback reason (frontend issue: PM-411)
A5: Update release checklist and runbook in Confluence and include the new 4-step smoke test before ramping above 5%
notes: We debated a purely-statistical anomaly detector vs explicit threshold-driven rules. For short term (this sprint) we’ll implement robust thresholds & combined signals; ML anomaly detector is a follow-up (ENG-53321) once datasets are collected.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance 1: Rollout controller supports combined latency+quality gating and a documented auto-rollback mode (toggleable)
Acceptance 2: Canary harness includes synthetic cases and is exercised in CI for every canary rollout job
Acceptance 3: Console dashboard surfaces canary health and last rollback reason; on-call can trigger rollback from console
Acceptance 4: Updated runbook deployed to Confluence with examples and checklist
